entities.summary: François-Marie, Marquess of Barthélemy was a French politician and diplomat who played a significant role in the French Revolution. Born on October 20, 1747, in Aubagne, France, he rose to prominence as a member of the French National Assembly, where he advocated for the rights of the common people and the abolition of feudalism. His leadership and oratory skills earned him the respect of his peers, and he became a key figure in the National Convention, where he worked closely with Maximilien Robespierre to establish the Committee of Public Safety. Barthélemy's legacy extends beyond his political career, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Enlightenment movement. He died on April 3, 1830, leaving behind a rich cultural heritage that continues to inspire artists and historians today.
